newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Two HK men sentenced to death for drugs in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Two HK men sentenced to death for drugs in Vietnam.

text.p: Two Hong Kong men were sentenced to death by a court in Vietnam on Friday for illegal trafficking in drugs, a court official said.
The two men, both holders of British passports, were arrested at Ho Chi Minh City airport in March 1996 after 18.1 kg (40 pounds) of heroin was found in their possession.
British diplomats confirmed the verdict for the two men, Sun Chi Kin and Chan Chun Hung Sammy, and said they had 15 days to appeal against the sentence.
Sun and Chan had been travelling with fake Portuguese passports and under false names when they were arrested, and the heroin found in their possession had been concealed in false-bottomed cases.

Diplomats said the authorities had granted consular access to the men for the first time last December. A consulate official who attended part of the one-day trial on Friday said she had spoken to them briefly before the hearing got under way.

A Hong Kong man was found guilty of a similar crime and executed in 1995. A Vietnamese-Canadian woman was sentenced to death last week in Hanoi after being found guilty of attempting to smuggle 5.45 kg (12 pounds) of heroin out of the country.
